memories.text: I rent a tiny place in Lyon on the slopes of Croix-Rousse, and climbing those stairs is my only cardio.
I run stability tests at Rhône Pharma, and the freezer room is colder than my ex.
Officially I'm a lab technician, pipettes and protocols all day long.
Rugby on a Saturday afternoon is sacred to me, and I never miss a home match at Gerland.
Answer me in French when possible, and keep it short.
My file says otherwise by mistake, but I'm not allergic to ibuprofen, I take it for migraines.
My brother Théo lives in Bordeaux and sends me wine I can't afford.
The lab cleaning rota is on Thursday evenings, which everyone hates.
Stability sampling goes like this: pull vials at 0, 3 and 6 months, store them at 25 degrees and 60 percent humidity, and run HPLC in duplicate.
I'm on Mistral, a project testing how a new vaccine holds up in hot climates.
Mistral is still a protocol draft, we're arguing about sampling intervals.
I joined the Croix-Rousse Choir, we rehearse every Tuesday in a church hall.
Did a road trip around Corsica in May, mountain roads with terrifying drops.
I'm allergic to mustard, which is tragic for someone from Dijon originally.
For tarte tatin I caramelise the apples in the pan first, lay the pastry on top, bake it, and flip it after ten minutes of rest.
Correction: the cleaning rota moved to Saturday mornings, even worse honestly.
My best friend's wedding will be in Annecy next June.
Mistral is owned by the Provence Health Institute, they fund the whole study.
Disaster on Mistral: a batch of samples got lost in shipping.
Walked through the Fête des Lumières with friends and the cathedral projections were magical.
The wedding moved to Biarritz because the groom's family is from the coast.
Our goldfish survived the winter in the drafty flat, against all odds.
I don't have a car, I bike everywhere, even in the rain.
Remind me to renew my health card before the end of January.
We moved to Marseille in June, and the light here is completely different.
I joined Calanque Biotech in June as a senior technician.
Calanque Biotech has its headquarters in Nice, but the labs are here.
My new manager is Hugo Lefèvre, a very calm chemist.
Hugo lives in Montpellier and takes the train in three days a week.
I applied for a PhD position in Grenoble, interviews are in September.
I've stopped following rugby; Formula 1 is my weekend obsession now.
We finally had the Mistral final report submitted to the institute last week.
Spent a week in Marrakech over the holidays, the souks were overwhelming.
I got the Grenoble PhD offer but turned it down, the new job is too good.
Choir warm-up: lip trills, sirens up and down, then the tongue twister about the archduchess's socks.
I've never been to Canada, even though half my cousins live in Quebec.
I love pottery, I throw bowls on a wheel every Sunday afternoon.
Remind me to pay the choir dues before the 1st of September.
